text:
Daily Faceoff called it plainly: Cole Hutson "has surprisingly emerged as one of the top rookies." The 20-year-old, a second-round pick and the younger brother of Montreal's Lane Hutson, has six goals and 16 points in 22 games for Washington, playing almost 20 minutes a night. Defensemen taken around his spot who stuck averaged 0.21 points a game in their first full season; he's at 0.73.

There's very little luck in it. His goals are close to his expected goals (6 on 4.7), and Washington's finishing with him on the ice is exactly where the chances say. At even strength, the Capitals take 57.26% of the shot attempts with him out there. He shoots a lot for a defenseman, 51 shots already, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in just six games, had 33% of his setups going across the royal road, against 4% for a typical defenseman. Our numbers project 57 points, in a wide range of 45 to 71.
headline: Cole Hutson is the rookie defenseman nobody expected
